decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 2 - The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building, unless otherwise shown on the approved plans.
Reason: In order to safeguard the appearance of the area.

Condition : 3 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: 12TG-300-01A, 12TG-301-03C, 12TG-301-02B, 12TG-301-04F, 12TG-301-05F, 12TG-301-01C, 12TG-301-06E, 12TG-300-02E and 12TG-302-01C, 210, 11, 220.
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 5 - (a) No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until a finalised Energy Strategy (demonstrating how the targets for carbon dioxide emissions reduction are to be met in line with the Mayor's energy hierarchy) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
(b) The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy and shall not commence above ground until full Design Stage calculations under the [Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method] have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority to show that the development will be constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, or any subsequent approved revisions.
Reason: In order to ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.

Condition : 6 - No development shall take place until the applicant has entered into a binding arrangement with the Council to make an agreed contribution to the Council's Carbon Offset Fund, in accordance with the zero carbon strategy set out in the Energy Statement hereby approved to an amount that equates to the shortfall in required energy savings to meet the 'zero carbon' target.
Reason: In order to ensure the development meets sustainability standards.

Condition : 7 - Prior to first occupation of the building(s) hereby approved, the development shall have been constructed to achieve an internal water use of 105 litres/person/day or less.
Reason: In order to protect and conserve water supplies and resources.

Condition : 8 - Secure covered cycle parking facilities (for not less than ten bicycles) for the occupants of, and two spaces for visitors to, the development shall be installed as shown on approved plan no. 11. The approved facilities shall conform to the current West trans West London Cycle Parking Guidance (or such other guidance as shall supersede it) in design and layout and be fully implemented and made available for use before the first occupation of the development or commencement of the approved use as appropriate and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 9 - The window(s) to be fitted on the side roof faces of the dwelling shall be black-framed and traditional, conservation-style.
Reason: In order to safeguard the architectural and historic interest of the conservation area.

Condition : 10 - No development shall take place until details of all new window frames and glazing bars, including samples if so required, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Such details shall indicate, at a scale of not less than 1:20, the longitudinal and cross-sectional detailing of new windows, sill and lintel detailing, and means of opening. All new window frames and glazing bars shall be of timber construction and white painted, with (if any) trickle vents concealed, and be retained as such thereafter. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In order to safeguard the architectural and historic interest of the listed building.

Condition : 11 - (a)	Prior to the commencement of works to form the approved pedestrian access within the existing boundary wall, details of the method of construction, including measures for the retention and protection of the wall, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved works shall be carried out in accordance with those details.

(b)	 Any bricks removed to facilitate the formation of the opening shall be carefully salvaged and retained for reuse within the boundary wall. In the event that any part of the wall is damaged, destabilised or collapses during the works, details of its repair or reconstruction, including the reuse of salvaged bricks and matching materials, shall first be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The repaired or reconstructed wall shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details and retained as such.

Reason: To ensure the retention and preservation of the boundary wall, safeguard the significance of the asset, and preserve the character and appearance of the Conservation Area.
description: Installation of one front boundary gate and new windows to allow the conversion of existing single family house to five self contained flats with associated refuse and cycle storage.
